body: @marcbaechinger @ojw28 Please could you take a look?
I think @christosts might have implemented the relevant changes, so is probably the best person to take a look.
i m getting continues crashes on firebase

In ExoPlayer version 2.12.0, there's a change in the downloads database table schema. The codepath indicated by the stack trace is executed when the player is upgrading the database to the latest version ([TABLE_VERSION = 3](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/r2.12.0/library/core/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/offline/DefaultDownloadIndex.java#L42)). The upgrade is executed only if the previous downloads database version is `2` and the table exists. The exception message indicates that column `title` is not found on the old table, but this column had to be present in the table in version 2 anyway.

May I ask:
- Did you update the ExoPlayer version recently to v2.12? If yes, from what version? 
- Is your app using any custom components for downloads, e.g. a custom DownloadIndex, or have you modified the database directly?
- Is your app using downloads from multiple threads? 
- Is the app creating multiple instances of `DownloadManager` and/or `DownloadService`?

 Did you update the ExoPlayer version recently to v2.12? If yes, from what version?

**Answer** 
yes, from 2.10.4 to 2.12.0

Please ensure that your app creates a single instance of `DownloadManager`, it is something that has come up again in the past, sometimes there are bugs in the app configuration (for example [issue 6516](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/issues/6516#issuecomment-648663819)).

The database upgrade is kicked-off by the constructor of the `DownloadManager` but it is executed in the `DownloadManager`'s background thread. One hypothesis could be that while the database is upgraded, the call to `getDownloadManager().downloadIndex.getDownload(url)` is introducing a race condition that is not properly handled.

Can you check if the call to `getDownloadManager().downloadIndex.getDownload(url)` happens before the `DownloadManager` is initialized? You can check if the `DownloadManager` is initialized with two ways: a direct call to [DownloadManager.isInitialized()](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/r2.12.0/library/core/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/offline/DownloadManager.java#L295) or adding a [DownloadManager.Listener](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/r2.12.0/library/core/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/offline/DownloadManager.java#L74) to the `DownloadManager` and overriding the [onInitialized](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/r2.12.0/library/core/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/offline/DownloadManager.java#L81) callback.

For debugging this, consider the following scenario: use your previous application version (the one using ExoPlayer r2.10.4) and download media (you may want to keep a back up of the database to repeat this test quickly, the database name is `exoplayer_internal.db`). Then update ExoPlayer to r.2.12.2 and start you application. When the app creates the `DownloadManager` instance, that should kick-off the database upgrade. At that point, please check whether calls to `getDownloadManager().downloadIndex.getDownload(url)` are happening before the `DownloadManager` is initialized, and if yes, try to wait until `DownloadManager` it is initialized before accessing the database with the `DownloadIndex`. 

In the meantime, I will try to replicate a similar scenario to see if the synchronisation around the database upgrade has any loop holes and needs further safeguarding.

Update: I can verify there is a race condition triggered if the app tries to access the database through `DownloadManager.downloadIndex` while the `DownloadManager` is still initialising. This should happen on first time the app updates from a version prior to 2.12 to a version after 2.12 and ExoPlayer had downloads in its database already. If the race condition is triggered, the player crashes with the same exception details. We will submit a fix and I will update the issue when the fix is commited and also available for use.

In the meantime, assuming your app is crashing because of this bug, please ensure that accessing to the database through the DownloadIndex happens after the `DownloadManager` is initialized (I listed a couple of ways onl the comment above).
Thank you so much for your quick support and assistance, i m trying to handle initialization issue, approx how much time it will take to fix from your side?
The commit should be in the dev-v2 branch within the week and we plan a minor release (2.12.3) within January.
